anchor: Who asserts it? Who has authority to admit it? Who is responsible for maintaining the invariant after admission? Those can be three different actors/bounded contexts.
statement: Argues Q2 ('who owns the commitment?') is itself badly framed since DDD does not require a single 'owner'; replaces it with three separable questions (who asserts it, who has authority to admit it, who maintains the invariant after admission) that may map to three different actors/bounded contexts, judged cleaner than debating whether Kernel/KnowledgeAggregate/KnowledgeEntity/KnowledgeContext 'owns' the commitment.

anchor: Is History actually a domain object, or is it the recorded consequence of domain events? ... History may simply be: Event Stream -> historical record, rather than something the aggregate conceptually owns as a mutable object.
statement: Reframes 'is History an Entity/VO?' into 'is History a domain object at all, or merely the recorded consequence of domain events (an event stream)?' -- proposing History may not be an aggregate-owned mutable object but simply the accumulated record of already-existing domain events.

anchor: A. A Knowledge Claim ... B. An Epistemic Determination ... C. A Coherent Epistemic Whole ... D. A Distinction-Preserving Record ... Conclusion: UNRESOLVED (repeated with 4-answer + cross-lens format across all 12 questions)
statement: Perplexity independently re-runs all 12 fundamental questions using the same four-candidate-answer-plus-cross-lens-plus-UNRESOLVED-conclusion method it used in S0367, reaching UNRESOLVED for every question (what is committed to, who owns it, identity's nature, evidence's nature, justification sufficiency, epistemic state's nature, confidence's nature, etc.), in direct contrast to DeepSeek's willingness in the same file to commit to concrete answers.

anchor: perform scenario-based falsification ... admission of a new claim, rejection, new evidence arriving, evidence invalidation, ... two claims sharing evidence, one claim having multiple evidence sources, evidence supporting many claims, conflicting evidence, unknown evidence, absent evidence ... A. Domain invariants ... F. Aggregate falsification ... G. Kernel boundary ... H. Remaining unknowns
statement: Closes with a detailed scenario-based falsification commission: for 14 named concepts ask 12 structural questions (what can/cannot change independently, what must be atomic vs. eventually consistent, what has independent lifecycle/identity, event/relationship/policy classification), then run 20 concrete lifecycle scenarios (admission, rejection, evidence invalidation, contestation, shared/conflicting/unknown/absent evidence, unresolved interpretation, missing justification, no applicable confidence, etc.) through 14 lenses with Zero applied specially to distinguish absent/unknown/unresolved/not-applicable/invalid/withdrawn/contradicted, producing 8 lettered outputs (invariants, independent lifecycles, shared lifecycles, cross-aggregate relationships, candidate boundaries, aggregate falsification, Kernel boundary, remaining unknowns) each classified ESTABLISHED/STRONGLY SUPPORTED/HYPOTHESIS/UNRESOLVED/FALSIFIED.

anchor: A justified claim. ... If a claim is part of KnowledgeOS, it must be justifiable -- there must exist evidence, a reasoning chain, and a constitutional determination that it belongs in the system. ... It does not require: Identity ... Epistemic state ... Confidence ... History
statement: Proposes 'a justified claim' as the smallest domain fact KnowledgeOS must protect, with the invariant that a claim in KnowledgeOS must be justifiable (evidence + reasoning chain + constitutional determination exist) -- explicitly not requiring identity, epistemic state, confidence, or history, reframing those as administrative/derived/assessment concerns rather than core invariant members.

anchor: Semantic relatedness and traceability do NOT imply transactional atomicity. ... Hypothesis FALSIFIED: The six parts do NOT require one aggregate.
statement: Runs a pairwise atomicity test across all six candidate aggregate members (Identity+Evidence, Identity+Justification, Identity+EpistemicState, Identity+Confidence, Identity+History, Evidence+Justification, EpistemicState+History), finding every pair has strong semantic relatedness/traceability but only WEAK-to-MODERATE transactional atomicity requirement, concluding the six-part KnowledgeAggregate hypothesis (established across S0363/S0365/S0366/S0368/S0369) is FALSIFIED because semantic relatedness and traceability do not imply transactional atomicity.

anchor: Epistemic state is derived. ... If state and history conflict, history wins. State is a convenience, not an authority. ... The Kernel should store events, not state.
statement: Concludes epistemic state is derived (not stored), with the event history as sole source of truth: if state and history ever conflict, history wins and state is a mere convenience projection, so the Kernel should record events and derive state on demand rather than persist state directly.

anchor: Confidence is an assessment output. ... The Kernel is the assigner, not the evaluator. ... History is an event stream. ... The Kernel should record events, preserve the event stream, never modify history.
statement: Resolves Confidence as an assessment output derived from external evidence/justification evaluation, with the Kernel as assigner-not-evaluator (assigns per constitutional rule but does not compute the underlying assessment); resolves History as an append-only event stream, never a mutable property, with the Kernel obligated to record and preserve but never modify it.

anchor: Evidence Reference | YES | The claim must link to its evidence ... Evidence Content | NO ... Evidence Identity | NO ... Evidence Provenance | NO ... Evidence Validity | NO ... Evidence Assessment | NO
statement: Splits Evidence into 6 sub-components (content, identity, reference, provenance, validity, assessment) and concludes only Evidence Reference must be co-located in the Kernel/aggregate; content/identity/provenance/validity/assessment all belong to the Evidence Context or Governance and remain outside.

anchor: Justification is a relation + argument structure. ... It is not a standalone object ... It is not an assessment (assessment is the evaluation of justification).
statement: Concludes Justification is neither a standalone object nor an assessment, but a relation-plus-argument-structure that only exists connecting evidence to claim; the Kernel should preserve the justification structure and relationship but never evaluate or interpret it (those belong to Governance/Interpretation contexts).

anchor: SUPERSEDED: Derived State + Relationship ... CONTESTED: Derived State + Relationship ... RECONCILED: Derived State + Relationship ... WITHDRAWN: Derived State (no relationship) ... INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: Derived State + Relationship + Assessment ... Epistemic states are derived from events and relationships. They are not stored independently.
statement: Gives concrete final classifications for the four contested lifecycle terms: SUPERSEDED/CONTESTED/RECONCILED are each Derived-State-plus-Relationship; WITHDRAWN is Derived-State-only (unilateral, no relationship); INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE is Derived-State-plus-Relationship-plus-Assessment -- resolving the state/relationship/event ambiguity these four terms carried since S0364.

anchor: Identity and History remain invariant across all transitions.
statement: Applying the Shiva-Shakti lens per transition (contested/superseded/withdrawn/reconciled/evidence-invalidated), finds Identity and History are the only elements that remain invariant across every single transition type, while evidence references and justification history remain invariant in most but not all (withdrawal keeps only identity+history).

anchor: A claim without evidence is a mere assertion -- not knowledge. ... A claim loses its justification. KnowledgeOS represents it as INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE or WITHDRAWN. ... The Kernel returns AMBIGUOUS or CONTRADICTION_DETECTED and refuses to execute. ... KnowledgeOS is not required to know something. It can represent absence of knowledge as a valid state.
statement: Applies the Zero lens to 8 absence scenarios (no evidence, no justification, unresolved meaning, no identity yet, evidence disappearing, two equal interpretations, no derivable state, nothing legitimately knowable), concluding each has a distinct legitimate non-knowledge representation (mere assertion, candidate, ephemeral candidate, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE/WITHDRAWN, UNRESOLVED/non-admission, AMBIGUOUS/CONTRADICTION_DETECTED refusal-to-execute, valid empty-knowledge state) rather than being forced into a knowledge state.

anchor: The smallest consistency boundary is: Identity + Evidence References + Justification History. ... Why these three? Identity is the anchor ... Evidence References are the link to justification ... Justification History is the record of how the claim became justified
statement: Replaces the falsified six-part aggregate with a narrower proposed consistency boundary of Identity + Evidence References + Justification History, with Epistemic State/Confidence/full Event History/Evidence Content/Justification Reasoning all pushed outside as derived/assessed/externally-owned.

The six-part invariant ... requires one aggregate FALSIFIED 2. Epistemic state is a stored property FALSIFIED 3. Confidence is a domain property FALSIFIED 4. History is aggregate state FALSIFIED
statement: Produces the batch's first full five-level classification ledger (8 ESTABLISHED findings, 6 STRONGLY SUPPORTED, 4 HYPOTHESIS, 8 UNRESOLVED, 4 explicitly FALSIFIED), formally retiring the six-part-aggregate, state-as-stored-property, confidence-as-domain-property, and history-as-aggregate-state claims.

anchor: we must not immediately recreate the same error one level lower. The correct question is: What invariant would become temporarily invalid if Identity, EvidenceReference, and JustificationHistory were changed independently? If we cannot produce such an invariant, we haven't proven the aggregate.
statement: Applies the same falsification standard just used to strike down the six-part aggregate against DeepSeek's own new replacement boundary (Identity+EvidenceRef+JustificationHistory), warning its justification is again a traceability argument rather than a demonstrated invariant, and explicitly refuses to accept it as more than a hypothesis pending the same rigor.

anchor: In DDD, identity is usually what distinguishes an Entity; it isn't necessarily itself the Entity. So: Claim -> ClaimId is conceptually more natural than: Identity Entity, Claim Content Entity.
statement: Challenges DeepSeek's classification of Identity as its own core Entity, noting standard DDD practice treats identity as an attribute distinguishing an Entity (Claim -> ClaimId) rather than identity itself being a separate Entity -- flagged provisional pending resolution of content mutability.

anchor: Claim #123 'The system uses PostgreSQL.' Later: 'The system uses PostgreSQL 17.' Is that Claim #123 amended or Claim #123 superseded by Claim #456? This changes: identity, history, evidence, justification, supersession, event model, aggregate boundary.
statement: Elevates claim-content mutability to the #1 open question with a concrete worked example (a claim's factual content is refined -- is it amendment or supersession by a new claim?), noting the answer cascades into identity, history, evidence, justification, supersession, the event model, and the aggregate boundary simultaneously, so the Kernel must not be built before this is settled.

anchor: 'Meaning is resolved before it becomes a candidate.' That potentially contradicts what we learned from the SNF/P5 research. P5 demonstrated that ambiguity and insufficient information are legitimate epistemic conditions, and that forcing interpretation is dangerous.
statement: Flags a tension between this file's Zero-lens claim that 'meaning is resolved before it becomes a candidate' and prior SNF/P5 findings that ambiguity and insufficient information are legitimate epistemic conditions and forced interpretation is dangerous; proposes instead that interpretation candidates may be resolved/ambiguous/insufficient, with only resolved ones proceeding to Kernel admission, while the wider KnowledgeOS ecosystem may still represent unresolved interpretation elsewhere.

anchor: 'The Kernel is the set of these gates.' I would mark this HYPOTHESIS, not established. ... Does the Kernel interpret, evaluate, apply, or merely enforce constitutional rules? ... The second would make the Kernel substantially more authoritative. I would strongly resist that unless evidence forces us there.
statement: Marks 'the Kernel is the set of admission gates' as an unestablished hypothesis and names the Kernel-interprets-vs-merely-enforces-the-Constitution question as one of the most important architectural forks still open, explicitly stating a preference to resist making the Kernel a constitutional interpreter unless evidence forces it.

anchor: 1. Evidence added ... 3. One evidence source supports 1,000 claims ... If one Evidence Entity is referenced by 1,000 claims, then changing evidence validity cannot require a single giant aggregate containing all claims. ... 9. Reconciliation ... Does C belong to A? B? Neither? All three? This could reveal the true bounded context structure.
statement: Proposes nine concrete falsification scenarios for the next research round to test whether the new Identity+EvidenceRef+JustificationHistory boundary is itself too large: evidence added/removed, one evidence source shared by 1000 claims (a strong argument against giant shared aggregates), one claim with 100 evidence references, justification-only changes, identity-before-admission, content-amendment-vs-supersession, contestation, and reconciliation producing a new claim C from conflicting A and B (whose ownership could reveal the true bounded-context structure).

anchor: The most important discovery is that the Kernel should not be designed by starting with a software component called 'Kernel.' Its boundary must emerge from the domain invariants that KnowledgeOS is constitutionally required to protect.
statement: States the phase's headline methodological conclusion: the Kernel must not be designed by starting from a named software component; its boundary must instead emerge from a 10-step derivation chain (Research -> Domain distinctions -> Domain scenarios -> Invariants -> Transactional consistency requirements -> Smallest consistency boundary -> Aggregate/Process boundary -> Kernel responsibility -> Logical Architecture -> Implementation).

anchor: Responsibility is not equivalent to aggregate ownership. The fact that something has constitutional responsibility does not prove that it must be an aggregate.
statement: Consolidates the ownership-reframing result: three distinct responsibilities (Claimant asserts, Governance defines admissibility rules, KnowledgeOS preserves the admitted record, with Kernel possibly enforcing invariants) must not be collapsed into a single 'aggregate owner', since constitutional responsibility does not by itself prove aggregate membership.

anchor: Evidence as shared Entity: Evidence E1 -> Claim A, Claim B, Claim C. This strongly argues against putting Evidence inside a KnowledgeClaim aggregate. ... Evidence as immutable snapshot / Value Object ... introduces duplication, sharing problems, and potentially unbounded aggregates.
statement: Consolidates the evidence-ownership question into two competing models -- Evidence as a shared Entity referenced by many claims (argues against embedding it in the claim aggregate) versus Evidence as an immutable per-claim snapshot Value Object (avoids atomicity problems but risks duplication and unbounded aggregates) -- leaving evidence ownership and grounding as one of the most important remaining Kernel questions.

anchor: Confidence has been substantially demoted from its original architectural importance. ... P5 demonstrated that apparently superior calibration could arise from coverage/abstention effects. ... Mechanism confidence != Domain confidence.
statement: Records that confidence has been demoted across the brainstorming phase from an assumed universal domain primitive to a possibly-Assessment concept, citing a prior P5 finding that apparently superior calibration can arise merely from coverage/abstention effects as a reason to keep mechanism confidence strictly distinct from domain confidence.

anchor: Dharma determines what must be protected; DDD determines where that protection belongs. ... Ganesha highlighted: The boundary / gate / threshold. This led to the possibility that the Kernel is fundamentally a boundary or admission mechanism, rather than necessarily an aggregate.
statement: Consolidates the division of labor across the full 11-lens stack used in this research phase (DDD as final adjudicator via 'aggregate boundaries follow consistency invariants, not conceptual relatedness'; Viveka for distinction preservation; Nyaya for claim/evidence/justification/determination separation; Navya-Nyaya for relations-as-first-class; Sanskrit-compiler for pipeline decomposition; Dharma for obligation-identification distinct from DDD's boundary-placement role; Rta for coherence-through-change; Shiva-Shakti for persistent-vs-changing separation; Ganesha for the boundary/gate/threshold framing of the Kernel; Godel for the external-verification safety constraint), summarizing each lens's distinct, non-overlapping contribution.

anchor: UNKNOWN != ABSENT ... UNRESOLVED != INVALID ... NOT_ASSESSED != LOW_CONFIDENCE ... NOT_APPLICABLE != UNKNOWN ... WITHDRAWN != FALSE ... NO_EVIDENCE != INVALID_EVIDENCE ... What does KnowledgeOS represent when there is nothing it can legitimately know? This question has become one of the most important unresolved Kernel questions.
statement: Formalizes the Zero lens as a permanent part of the methodology (distinct role from other lenses: detecting hidden collapses of absence/undefined/unrepresented/assumed-away conditions) and consolidates six named non-collapse pairs it has produced (UNKNOWN!=ABSENT, UNRESOLVED!=INVALID, NOT_ASSESSED!=LOW_CONFIDENCE, NOT_APPLICABLE!=UNKNOWN, WITHDRAWN!=FALSE, NO_EVIDENCE!=INVALID_EVIDENCE), elevating 'what does KnowledgeOS represent when there is nothing it can legitimately know' to one of the most important unresolved Kernel questions.

anchor: KnowledgeOS must protect the integrity and accountability of admitted knowledge without becoming the authority that determines semantic truth.
statement: States the emerging core architectural principle of the entire brainstorming phase: KnowledgeOS must protect the integrity and accountability of admitted knowledge without becoming the authority that determines semantic truth, implying a strict pipeline separation from Interpretation through Candidate generation, Evidence/justification, Governance determination, Knowledge admission, to Historical preservation.

anchor: Candidate != Knowledge -- STRONGLY SUPPORTED ... Six-part KnowledgeAggregate -- FALSIFIED ... KnowledgeClaim as Aggregate Root -- UNRESOLVED ... Kernel = Aggregate -- UNRESOLVED ... Kernel = Process/Boundary -- UNRESOLVED ... Kernel implementation -- NOT AUTHORIZED
statement: Consolidates a 24-row status ledger across the whole phase: 7 non-collapse distinctions rated STRONGLY SUPPORTED, the six-part KnowledgeAggregate rated FALSIFIED, KnowledgeClaim-as-domain-concept a STRONG HYPOTHESIS, most other classifications (Evidence-in-aggregate, Justification-as-VO, Kernel=Aggregate-vs-Process, event sourcing) UNRESOLVED or HYPOTHESIS, and explicitly states Kernel implementation is NOT AUTHORIZED at this stage.

anchor: no Kernel implementation; no programming-language decision; no database schema; no event-sourcing commitment; no API design; no final aggregate design; no KnowledgeClaim aggregate implementation; no SNF reopening; no real-language corpus experiment; no promotion of an SNF mechanism into KnowledgeOS. The P5 closure remains intact.
statement: Issues an explicit 10-item 'what we should NOT do yet' list closing off Kernel implementation, language/database/event-sourcing/API decisions, final aggregate design, and any reopening of the closed P5/SNF research track, reaffirming the P5 closure remains intact and separate from this Kernel discovery thread.

statement: Expands the falsification-round scenario list from the 9 in S0370 to 24 concrete domain scenarios (admission, rejection, evidence lifecycle events, justification revision, confidence reassessment, content change, supersession/contestation/reconciliation/withdrawal, absence/unknown cases, duplicate-identity attempts, contradictory determination, admission replay, shared/multiple evidence sources, unresolved interpretations), each to be run through a 9-question checklist (what changes, what must change atomically, what may change independently, what invariant is protected, what relation/event/state/policy results, what remains outside the boundary) before the lenses are applied.

anchor: What is the smallest domain consistency boundary required to preserve an admitted knowledge commitment without making the Kernel responsible for semantic interpretation, evidence ownership, or truth itself?
statement: Names the single most important unresolved architectural question carried forward from this consolidation: what is the smallest domain consistency boundary required to preserve an admitted knowledge commitment without making the Kernel responsible for semantic interpretation, evidence ownership, or truth itself.

anchor: The commitment is to a governed epistemic object defined by six constituents ... The commitment is an Aggregate concern realized through the KnowledgeClaim Entity (Aggregate Root).
statement: Q1 answer names the commitment object 'KnowledgeClaim' and asserts it is the Aggregate Root realizing a six-constituent governed epistemic object (identity, epistemic state, confidence, justification structure, evidence grounding, historical provenance) -- the critique later rejects the Aggregate-Root classification as premature since only 'important domain concept' has been demonstrated, not the aggregate invariant.

anchor: UNRESOLVED -- CRITICAL: Is Evidence an Entity (shareable across multiple claims) or a Value Object (immutable snapshot unique to this claim)? ... This is the central unresolved aggregate boundary question that determines the Kernel's shape.
statement: Names Evidence's Entity-vs-Value-Object status the central unresolved aggregate-boundary question: as a shared Entity it cannot be inside the KnowledgeClaim aggregate (evidence-grounding becomes procedural, not atomic); as a per-claim Value Object snapshot it can be inside but cannot be shared and risks an unbounded aggregate.

anchor: 1 Single-gate ... 2 Identity uniqueness ... 3 Evidence-grounding ... 4 Justification immutability ... 5 Sufficiency-at-admission ... 6 Historical completeness ... 7 No mechanism identity ... 8 No mechanism confidence ... 9 Representation-agnosticism ... 10 Non-admission exclusion ... these invariants are constitutional postulates ... statement: Formalizes a numbered 10-item constitutional invariant table (single-gate, identity uniqueness, evidence-grounding, justification immutability, sufficiency-at-admission, historical completeness, no-mechanism-identity, no-mechanism-confidence, representation-agnosticism, non-admission-exclusion), each tagged with what protects it, and frames them via the Godel lens as constitutional postulates the Kernel enforces but cannot itself establish or prove complete.

anchor: Supersession | Relationship + Domain Event | 'A supersedes B' is a relation ... Retraction | Domain Event + State transition ... Contestation | Derived condition ... exists when an unresolved Challenge entity/relationship is present. It is NOT a state of the knowledge claim. ... Reconciliation | Domain Event + Relationship
statement: Gives a concrete final classification for the four lifecycle transitions, explicitly noting they are NOT mentioned by the existing constitutional law and are speculative extensions: Supersession = Relationship+Event; Retraction = Event+State transition; Contestation = a Derived condition dependent on an unresolved Challenge entity, never a claim state itself; Reconciliation = Event+Relationship.

anchor: A. Minimal State Aggregate ... B. Immutable Snapshot Aggregate ... C. Event-Sourced Stream (Smallest Possible) ... D. Dual Aggregate (DDD Pure) ... Roots: KnowledgeClaim + Evidence as separate aggregates ... Risk: Cross-aggregate invariants (evidence-grounding, sufficiency) cannot be atomic.
statement: Proposes four fully specified candidate consistency-boundary architectures with explicit contents and risks: A Minimal State Aggregate (Identity+EpistemicState+Confidence+History only, evidence/justification external, making evidence-grounding merely procedural); B Immutable Snapshot Aggregate (adds VO snapshots of Justification/Evidence, risking duplication/unbounded size); C Event-Sourced Stream (smallest possible, aggregate IS the event stream); D Dual Aggregate (KnowledgeClaim and Evidence as separate DDD-pure aggregates, risking non-atomic cross-aggregate invariants).

anchor: Evidence-grounding | Requires Evidence Inside? Yes (to enforce atomically) | Cannot share evidence; aggregate bloat ... Representation-agnosticism | Yes (to avoid coupling) | Pushes evidence outside
statement: Names an explicit tension between two constitutional invariants: evidence-grounding wants evidence physically inside the aggregate for atomic enforcement, while representation-agnosticism wants evidence pushed outside to avoid coupling -- left UNRESOLVED as to whether constitutional integrity requires atomic containment or a merely procedural admission-time guarantee is sufficient.

anchor: How does the Kernel preserve meaning distinctions without interpreting meaning? The Vani lens requires preserving artha while discarding sabda, but the Kernel has no access to meaning. This is the boundary paradox.
statement: Names a 'boundary paradox': the Kernel is required by the Vani lens to preserve meaning (artha) while discarding raw expression (sabda), yet the Kernel by design has no access to meaning at all -- left as an unresolved architectural puzzle.

anchor: Domain concept != Entity != Aggregate Root != Consistency boundary != Kernel. The research currently sometimes moves between these as though they were equivalent. They aren't.
statement: Names a chain of five distinct concepts (Domain concept, Entity, Aggregate Root, Consistency boundary, Kernel) that the source document treats as though interchangeable, warning this conflation is a recurring methodological error across the whole research thread.

anchor: Evidence E1 supports Claim A, supports Claim B, contradicts Claim C. If E1 is an Entity, putting E1 inside Claim A's aggregate becomes impossible. ... KnowledgeClaim -> EvidenceReference + JustificationStructure -> Evidence Context ... a strong argument against evidence-containing aggregates.
statement: Uses the Nyaya/Navya-Nyaya relational reading (evidence->justification->claim as a relational structure, not ownership) to construct a concrete counterexample -- one Evidence entity simultaneously supporting Claim A, supporting Claim B, and contradicting Claim C -- as a strong argument that KnowledgeClaim aggregates should hold only EvidenceReference+JustificationStructure, never Evidence itself.

anchor: Viveka should also be applied to: Kernel != Aggregate, Aggregate != Bounded Context, Policy != Rule, Assessment != State, Event != Relationship, Admission != Interpretation. ... this is the missing second-order Viveka analysis.
statement: Extends the Viveka distinction-preservation discipline to a 'second-order' level, proposing six further architectural-vocabulary distinctions that must not collapse: Kernel!=Aggregate, Aggregate!=Bounded Context, Policy!=Rule, Assessment!=State, Event!=Relationship, Admission!=Interpretation.

anchor: Dharma identifies what must be protected; DDD determines where that protection belongs. ... The fact that something has a constitutional duty does not prove that it must be an aggregate. Otherwise we'd make every constitutional responsibility an aggregate.
statement: Reasserts and sharpens the Dharma/DDD division of labor first raised in S0371 (dharma identifies obligation, DDD decides placement), warning that treating every constitutional duty as automatically implying an aggregate would make every responsibility in the system an aggregate.

anchor: The document is dangerously close to making: coherence -> event sourcing. That inference is not justified. ... Event sourcing is an implementation/model choice.

anchor: 'Where does epistemic accountability become a domain fact, and what is the smallest boundary that can enforce that transition without becoming the authority for interpretation or truth?' ... statement: Reframes the whole research programme's real question as 'where does epistemic accountability become a domain fact, and what is the smallest boundary that can enforce that transition without becoming the authority for interpretation or truth', and states what it judges the single key architectural lesson emerging from the entire research programme so far: do not confuse accountability, coherence, traceability, and semantic relatedness with transactional ownership.

anchor: Give it these cases: 1. Candidate admitted ... 20. Contradictory determination ... force each lens to answer only: 1. What distinction must be preserved? ... 6. What does the lens NOT prove? Then DDD performs the final synthesis. ... Scenario | Must be atomic | May be independent | Boundary implication
statement: Recommends a 'Cross-Lens Aggregate Falsification Round' organized around 20 concrete scenarios rather than concepts, with every lens (DDD, Vani/compiler, Paninian, Nyaya, Navya-Nyaya, Viveka, Dharma, Rta, Ganesha, Shiva-Shakti, Godel, Zero) constrained to answer only 6 fixed questions per scenario (including explicitly 'what does the lens NOT prove?'), followed by a decision matrix (scenario x must-be-atomic x may-be-independent x boundary-implication) with DDD synthesis performed last and only after the matrix is filled -- explicitly reversing the prior order of classify-then-scenario-test.

statement: Restates the governing invariant for the candidate-declaration mechanism: a process may discover and declare its own runtime identity, but may never self-select the role, scope, work item, or authority it is to hold -- those must come from the authoritative commission (AST-018 next-actor), with a MISMATCH between the prompt's claimed role and the commission's role forcing STOP (GO-08).
invariants: self-bind identity only, never self-choose role/scope/work-item/authority

anchor: Per ES-004.3, historical/decision text is never rewritten -- the correction is recorded as an additive annotation, and the fresh reviewer consumes it before the prompt body.
statement: Demonstrates the ES-004.3 discipline in practice: when a verbatim preserved prompt later states a workflow fact that a subsequent governed act (a human CONTINUATION) supersedes, the correction is recorded as an additive 'STATE SUPERSESSION NOTICE' section placed before the original prompt body, and the original verbatim text is left completely unchanged.

anchor: F-3 is disclosed as aggravating, not exculpatory: producing this record adds a further participating act by 77b85fa3 on this work item. If the PO/ARB's ruling turns on 'has this process already acted here,' this record is itself part of the evidence against it.
statement: A candidate for an independence-sensitive review role discloses that the very act of writing its own declaration record is itself a further participating act that could count against its own independence, explicitly refusing to treat its own record-production as exculpatory -- an instance of radical self-disclosure over self-serving interpretation.

anchor: Do not decide for yourself that read-only orientation is or is not participation if the governing policy is ambiguous. Report the factual evidence. The candidate therefore returned UNDETERMINED and stopped, rather than self-certifying under reading B.
statement: Establishes a governance behavioral principle: when a governing policy is deliberately left as a placeholder and genuinely ambiguous, the correct response for a self-assessing process is to report factual evidence and return UNDETERMINED rather than adjudicate the ambiguity in its own favor, escalating the open question to the PO/ARB with named legitimate dispositions instead of a recommendation.

anchor: IMPLEMENTED != VERIFIED != ADOPTED != AUTHORIZED (§38) -- this review establishes readiness for the fourth-to-third transition and leaves ADOPTED and AUTHORIZED untouched.
statement: Confirms and applies the four-state lifecycle model (IMPLEMENTED, VERIFIED, ADOPTED, AUTHORIZED as four distinct, non-collapsible states, §38) as load-bearing governance vocabulary: a PASS review moves work from VERIFIED toward being ready for the ADOPTED decision, but does not itself adopt or authorize, and the adoption decision belongs solely to the PO/ARB.

anchor: F-2 | Decision required (scope boundary) | The work item now carries a fourth asset -- AST-019/ActivateCommissionedFreshSession -- that is IMPLEMENTED ... but NOT VERIFIED (producer bar) and outside the verification report ... The adoption decision must name its scope explicitly.
statement: Finds that an additional asset (AST-019) landed on the same work item after the original three-layer verification was completed, and warns that adopting 'the work item' without explicitly excluding this unverified fourth asset would silently sweep an unverified capability into adoption -- the adoption decision must name its scope explicitly.

anchor: F-3 ... AST-019's implementing session held no registered lane on this work item, and its runtime identity is recorded nowhere by UUID ... the producer bar for AST-019's future verification is not mechanically enforceable -- there is no recorded producer identity to exclude
statement: Identifies a governance-model gap: because AST-019's implementing session never registered a lane or recorded its runtime identity, the producer-verifier separation principle cannot be mechanically enforced for its future verification (no producer identity exists to exclude), and the operating model as written has no lane-shape at all for a human-authorized amendment slice landing on a STOPPED work item.
missing: a defined lane-shape for human-authorized amendment slices on stopped items

anchor: F-4 ... every lane on this work item ... was created by hand-composed AST-015 append calls in governance-recording capacity, not through appoint ... appoint auto-generates a thin executionContext ... and cannot carry the disclosure depth the estate's own precedent requires
statement: Observes that in practice every lane transition on this work item was created by hand-composed governance-recording rather than the documented `appoint` mechanism, because `appoint` cannot yet carry the disclosure depth (enumerated bars, prior participation, exposure, preservation conditions, non-actions) the estate's own precedent requires -- meaning the operating model's documented §8 path is not the path actually taken, pending either a disclosure passthrough for `appoint` or sanctioning hand-composition as the disclosure-heavy path.

anchor: F-6 ... The §29 CASE 6 presentation ... is unreachable from the record when the review lane closes with STOP ... manufacturing a CONTINUATION to make the tooling render more nicely is self-directed workflow manipulation with no human direction behind it.
statement: Finds a structural gap where the workflow engine's own 'ready for adoption' presentation (CASE 6) can only render from a COMPLETED lane, never from one closed via STOP -- yet the declared review sequence and every precedent prescribe closing review lanes with STOP -- and explicitly refuses to repair this by manufacturing an unauthorized CONTINUATION merely to make the tooling render more nicely, naming that as self-directed workflow manipulation with no human direction behind it.
missing: a settled choice between STOP and COMPLETE for delivered reviews
invariants: append-only record, STOPPED is sticky (Inv E)

anchor: The model was thereby exercised on its own adoption review -- the strongest available evidence of the §39 success criterion: the human said one business sentence, and no workflow mechanics were required of them.
statement: Reports that re-executing the model's own live `outcome`/`session` commands during this very review (rather than trusting the verifier's report) reproduced identical or improved results and constitutes the strongest available evidence for the design's §39 success criterion -- a human issuing one business-language sentence with no workflow mechanics required of them.

experiment.setup: re-execute the live outcome/session commands against the real workflow state during the reviewer's own adoption review of the same model
experiment.method: direct re-execution rather than trusting the verifier's report
experiment.result: outcome and session render correctly against the reviewer's own lane with no exposed mechanics; test suite counts matched or exceeded verifier's report
experiment.interpretation: the model successfully governed the process used to review it
experiment.conclusion: treated as the strongest available evidence for the §39 success criterion

anchor: The human speaks BUSINESS LANGUAGE. The system handles TECHNICAL WORKFLOW MECHANICS. The human never operates the workflow engine.
statement: States the operating model's one-line core principle, operationalized across all 40 sections: the human speaks business language and makes business/authority decisions; the system (Governance/Communication capabilities via the canonical workflow mechanism) performs all mechanical consequences; the human is never required to understand workflow UUIDs, REGISTER/HANDOFF/START, mutationOwner, predecessor, transition JSON, or internal resolver codes.

anchor: The Governance Engineer is the dedicated human-facing governance responsibility (not a new workflow role, not a service, not a position -- adopted six-role operating model, 2026-08-19). ... The Communication Engineer is NOT a permanent person -- it is a transferable operational responsibility.
statement: Defines the Governance Engineer (dedicated human-facing responsibility for intake, classification, substantive governance decisions, escalation, and adoption presentation) and the Communication Engineer (a transferable operational responsibility any authorized actor may perform for routine coordination, but never for substantive governance decisions) as responsibilities rather than new workflow roles, services, or positions -- citing the six-role operating model adopted 2026-08-19 as the source of this non-equivalence rule.

anchor: CONTINUE / PERMISSION_REQUIRED / FRESH_SESSION_REQUIRED / GOVERNANCE_DECISION_REQUIRED / STOP ... a business rendering of the existing governed/application result model -- never a second workflow-state vocabulary, never a new state machine.
statement: Defines the five business-level session-completion outcomes (CONTINUE, PERMISSION_REQUIRED, FRESH_SESSION_REQUIRED, GOVERNANCE_DECISION_REQUIRED, STOP), explicitly constrained to be a business-language rendering of the existing governed/application result model rather than a new second workflow-state vocabulary or state machine.

anchor: role != process identity, identity != eligibility, eligibility != appointment, appointment != activation, activation != authorization ... A process identity is DISCOVERED FROM THE RUNTIME -- never invented by the human, copied from another session, inferred from prompt text, or chosen from a human-entered UUID.
statement: Formalizes a six-link non-collapse chain of governance-identity concepts (role != process identity != eligibility != appointment != activation != authorization), each a genuinely separate step, and the rule that process identity is always discovered from the runtime, never supplied, copied, inferred, or human-chosen.

anchor: Human authority must never be manufactured. The system may prepare the transition, validate preconditions, explain the consequence, prepare the activation -- it must not fabricate a human act.
statement: States the 'Human START boundary' invariant (G-3): the system may prepare and validate a role transition but must never fabricate the human authorization act itself; business-language framing ('Start the assigned session') is used instead of exposing the technical transition command.

anchor: MATCH -> ACTOR_MATCH -> 'This is the assigned session. You may continue.' MISMATCH -> ACTOR_MISMATCH -> 'This is not the session assigned to this work.' ... Do not: create another appointment, replace the appointed actor, impersonate the appointed actor, self-register, or treat the mismatch as authorization.
statement: Defines the fresh-session-with-existing-appointment protocol: compare expected actor to current runtime identity yielding MATCH ('you may continue') or MISMATCH ('not the assigned session' with recovery options), and explicitly forbids five self-serving responses to a mismatch (creating another appointment, replacing the appointed actor, impersonating it, self-registering, or treating the mismatch itself as authorization).

anchor: Provide a session UUID, choose runtime process identity, determine mutationOwner, determine predecessor, construct REGISTER, construct HANDOFF, construct START, edit workflow JSON, invoke workflow-state.php, inspect workflow records to route the work, diagnose INV-B, diagnose G-3, understand token/tokenRef, manually calculate authorization. If the human is forced to do any of these ... the implementation has failed the human-facing contract.
statement: Enumerates 14 hard acceptance criteria the human must never be forced to perform (session UUIDs, mutationOwner/predecessor, constructing REGISTER/HANDOFF/START, editing workflow JSON, diagnosing invariants, understanding tokenRef, manually calculating authorization), declaring the implementation failed if any occur in a normal workflow.

statement: Originates the four-state completion model (IMPLEMENTED / VERIFIED / ADOPTED / AUTHORIZED) as a required, never-collapsed distinction in the implementing session's completion report -- the same model later confirmed and applied throughout S0374-S0382.

statement: Formalizes a 10-term DDD responsibility vocabulary for the governance/communication domain (Work Item, Role, Assignment, Role Transition, Human Decision, Next Actor Recommendation, Session Continuity, Governance Engineer, Communication Engineer, Reviewer) and the closing non-collapse rule Role != Session != Process Identity != Authority.

anchor: AST-015 remains the SINGLE WORKFLOW AUTHORITY ... AST-017 remains READ-ONLY ... AST-018 is NEXT-ACTOR ORCHESTRATION ... it must not become a second workflow engine, an identity authority, an adoption authority, a migration engine, EKS-07.
statement: Defines the boundaries of the three existing mechanisms this operating model is layered over without replacing: AST-015 (single workflow authority, no parallel store), AST-017 (read-only, on-demand governed-state resolution, never creates assignments or fabricates authority), and AST-018 (next-actor orchestration answering 'what should happen next', explicitly forbidden from becoming a second workflow engine, identity authority, adoption authority, or migration engine).

anchor: No grant on the workflow record. The engine's grants vocabulary is lane write-authority, not asset authorization. Recording this authorization there would invent semantics the mechanism does not have (ES-005.4), so grants remains []. The authoritative home of this authorization is this document.
statement: Distinguishes the engine's 'grants' vocabulary (lane write-authority) from 'asset authorization' (an artifact being approved for future use), refusing to record the authorization decision inside the mechanical workflow record because doing so would invent semantics the mechanism does not have; the governance document itself, not the workflow engine, is the authoritative home of this authorization fact.

anchor: F-8 | The workflow engine has no vocabulary for ADOPTED or AUTHORIZED -- both live only in governance documents, so no mechanism can answer 'is this authorized?' | Observation for a future increment; not repaired here, since inventing a state would breach §26/§37
statement: Records a new finding F-8: the mechanical workflow engine has no vocabulary at all for ADOPTED or AUTHORIZED -- both concepts exist only in governance documents, so no mechanism query can answer whether an artifact is authorized; explicitly deferred as a future-increment observation rather than repaired opportunistically, since inventing a new state would breach the no-scope-expansion and AST-015-boundary rules.

anchor: F-6 . F-7 ... Verified empirically on a copy of the record: closing the governance lane with STOP short-circuits to WORK_ITEM_STOPPED; closing it with COMPLETE instead makes the renderer state 'The implementation actor is assigned and waiting,' because predecessor lanes stay permanently HANDED_OFF. statement: Empirically confirms on a copy of the real workflow record (not just theoretically, as in S0376's F-6) that the CASE-6 'ready for adoption' presentation token is unreachable through any real governed multi-lane flow: STOP short-circuits before reaching it, and COMPLETE instead produces a false 'implementation actor waiting' state because predecessor lanes remain permanently HANDED_OFF; only a test fixture that directly constructs every lane as COMPLETED can produce the token, meaning the contract test is honest given its input but does not prove the token is reachable from real governed flow.

lineage_claims.target: finding F-6 in the Governance Adoption Review (S0376)
lineage_claims.quote: the adoption presentation this very decision exercised -- is not machine-rendered under the estate's closure discipline

experiment.hypothesis: the workflow engine can machine-render the CASE-6 adoption presentation from a real governed multi-lane record
experiment.setup: take a copy of the actual KOS-OPERATING-MODEL-001 workflow record and close the governance lane two different ways
experiment.inputs: a copied real workflow record with the same lane history
experiment.method: close the governance lane with STOP in one branch and COMPLETE in another, then query the renderer
experiment.result: STOP short-circuits to WORK_ITEM_STOPPED before reaching CASE 6; COMPLETE renders a false 'implementation actor waiting' state because predecessor lanes remain HANDED_OFF
experiment.interpretation: CASE 6 is only reachable when every lane is directly constructed as COMPLETED, which never happens in real governed flow
experiment.limitations: tested on a copy, not the live record; only two closure paths tested
experiment.conclusion: CASE 6 is not machine-renderable from any real governed flow; flagged as an AST-018 follow-up, not a defect in the adopted layers

anchor: Basis: PROVENANCE ATTRIBUTION -- not self-declaration. The producer never declared this identity in any governed artifact. It is attributed here by a third party from runtime evidence. ...
